$comment: Licence policy for dependencies we distribute (ADR-0016). Development-only tooling
is out of scope — it never ships. Adding an entry here is a deliberate, reviewed
decision: it asserts the licence is compatible with distributing this AGPL-3.0 work.
allowed: GNU Lesser General Public License v3 or later (LGPLv3+)

rationale.MIT-0: cffi (via argon2-cffi, the password hasher). MIT with the attribution clause removed — strictly more permissive than MIT, which is already allowed, so nothing about distribution changes.
rationale.LGPL-3.0-only: psycopg and its helpers. The LGPL explicitly permits use by, and distribution with, a (A)GPL-3.0 work; we link it unmodified and ship its source availability notice.
rationale.MPL-2.0: lightningcss (via Tailwind). File-level copyleft: MPL-2.0 §3.3 permits distribution as part of a larger AGPL-3.0 work provided the MPL-covered files stay under the MPL.
rationale.Mozilla Public License 2.0 (MPL 2.0): certifi (via httpx, in the extractor SDK). The same licence as the entry above, spelled as a classifier rather than as an SPDX id — the substance, and the reasoning, are identical.
rationale.Apache Software License; MIT License: uvloop declares both; either alone is compatible.
rationale.GNU Lesser General Public License v3 or: pyvips-binary, the wheel that carries libvips for `preview-gen`. Same substance as the LGPL-3.0-only entry above, spelled as a classifier: the LGPL permits use by, and distribution with, an (A)GPL-3.0 work. We ship it unmodified, load it through its own binding, and keep its source-availability notice.
rationale.AGPL-3.0-only: This project's own licence (ADR-0016). A dependency under the same terms as the work that distributes it needs no further reasoning — and the AGPL is why PyMuPDF's decision tree is available to us at all without a commercial licence.

python:colorama.reason: Windows-only conditional dependency (sys_platform == 'win32'), so its metadata is absent on the Linux and macOS hosts that run this check. Declared here to keep the verdict identical on every platform.

python:tzdata.reason: Windows-only conditional dependency; same reasoning as colorama.

python:pypdfium2.reason: PDFium (Google) is BSD-3-Clause; the binding adds Apache-2.0 parts and the wheel's metadata states both as free text rather than an SPDX expression, which this gate cannot read. Both licences are already allowed above; the entry records the reading rather than granting anything new.

python:pymupdf.reason: PyMuPDF is dual-licensed: AGPL-3.0 or an Artifex commercial licence, and its metadata says so as free text rather than as an SPDX expression. This project is AGPL-3.0-only, so the open half is the one that applies and nothing about distribution changes — which is also why it was chosen over a permissively licensed PDF text extractor with a worse decision tree (05 § built-in extractors).
